frameworks.name: Promo (the playbook)
frameworks.what: A promo or launch film: the offer or a tension, proof of the product doing the thing, the signature moment, the offer, the close

beats.name: Hook
beats.job: The offer, or a tension the viewer recognises, spoken and on screen

beats.name: Turn
beats.job: Why now, or what changes

beats.name: Proof
beats.job: Three moments of the product doing the thing, each an ask, a result and a hold

beats.name: Peak
beats.job: The signature moment

beats.name: Offer
beats.job: Price or promise, once, in the fixed wording

beats.name: Close
beats.job: Call to action, a deadline if any, the logo

frameworks.notes: From knowledge/playbooks/promo.md. Under about 25 s the hook and close take most of the film: use a short-form framework instead.

frameworks.name: Demo (the playbook)
frameworks.what: A product demo: the finished result first, the job, three steps of one continuous story, the payoff, the close

beats.name: Result first
beats.job: Show the finished outcome, then say here is how

beats.name: The job
beats.job: Who needs this and what they are trying to get done, in one line

beats.name: Three steps
beats.job: Each step an ask, a result and a hold; one story, one set of data

beats.name: Payoff
beats.job: Return to the finished outcome, now understood

beats.name: Close
beats.job: What to do next, the logo

frameworks.name: Tutorial (the playbook)
frameworks.what: A tutorial: the promise shown finished, what you need, chapters of one sub-task each, the recap, what next

beats.name: Promise
beats.job: What you will have made by the end, shown finished

beats.name: What you need
beats.job: Only if something is needed first

beats.name: Chapters
beats.job: One sub-task each, 20 to 45 s, each with a title card of two to four words

beats.name: Recap
beats.job: The finished thing again, and the steps named

beats.name: Next
beats.job: Where to go from here, the logo

frameworks.notes: From knowledge/playbooks/tutorial.md. Chapters take whatever the other beats leave.

frameworks.name: Edit of footage (minimal)
frameworks.what: An edit of raw footage: the hook taken from the footage, the story, a close. The edit playbook sets the approvals, not a shape, so this is only the frame around the story

beats.name: Hook
beats.job: The angle: the strongest moment or line of the footage, first

beats.name: Story
beats.job: The kept lines in order, covered with inserts and titles

beats.name: Close
beats.job: What to do next, the logo

frameworks.notes: The edit playbook gives no shape; the paper edit decides the story. A borrowed framework can be used when the footage allows it.

frameworks.name: Pain, reframe, promise
frameworks.what: Conversion films: ads, landing-page hero videos, conversion-focused social.

beats.name: Pain
beats.job: Name the audience's real problem in their own words; the hook is its first 2 s.

beats.name: Reframe
beats.job: Flip the problem so the viewer sees it differently.

beats.name: Promise
beats.job: Show life on the other side, specific and time-bound; the CTA is its last seconds.

frameworks.notes: Shares are the 30 s version; the CTA window comes from timing-rules (3-4 s at 15, 4-6 s at 30, 6-10 s at 60). Sizes are the source's timings, allowed 25% either way.

frameworks.name: World, hero, transformation
frameworks.what: Product launches, brand films and anchor pieces.

beats.name: World
beats.job: Set the context: who lives here and what is broken.

beats.name: Hero
beats.job: The product, founder or method arrives; show what it does.

beats.name: Transformation
beats.job: The world changes; before and after at scale, carrying the CTA.

frameworks.notes: No 30 s timing is given; shares are the equal thirds of the 60 and 90 s versions, and the 15 s version is front-loaded. Sizes are the source's timings, allowed 25% either way.

frameworks.name: Founder explainer
frameworks.what: A person speaking to camera: founder content, thought leadership, personal brand.

beats.name: Hook
beats.job: One-line provocation.

beats.name: Stakes
beats.job: Why this matters.

beats.name: Insight
beats.job: The actual point.

beats.name: Proof
beats.job: One concrete example or data point.

beats.name: CTA
beats.job: What to do next, narrow and specific.

frameworks.notes: The source times hook, stakes and insight only; proof and CTA spans are my fill using its CTA length rule, and at 15 s five beats compress to four. Sizes are the source's timings, allowed 25% either way.

frameworks.name: Content spiral
frameworks.what: Kinetic typography and opinion pieces that zoom inward then snap back.

beats.name: Wide claim
beats.job: State the headline take.

beats.name: Zoom one
beats.job: One layer of nuance.

beats.name: Zoom two
beats.job: The layer underneath that.

beats.name: Snap-back
beats.job: Return to the wide claim, reframed by the zooms.

frameworks.notes: Each zoom runs 1.5 to 2 times faster than the one before; only the 15 s timing is given, so scaling to other lengths is unverified. Sizes are the source's timings, allowed 25% either way.

frameworks.name: Educational demo
frameworks.what: How-to, tutorial and training films built around one technique.

beats.name: Problem state
beats.job: Show what someone is stuck on.

beats.name: Reveal
beats.job: Show the technique or trick.

beats.name: Walk-through
beats.job: Apply it step by step.

beats.name: Result
beats.job: The after-state, side by side with before.

frameworks.notes: One technique per 15 s; a second technique needs a longer cut. Only the 15 s timing is given. Sizes are the source's timings, allowed 25% either way.

frameworks.name: Energy curve (hook, build, apex, release, CTA)
frameworks.what: A pacing overlay for any short film, placing the energy peak two-thirds in.

beats.name: Hook
beats.job: First 2 s, high contrast with the shot that follows.

beats.name: Build
beats.job: Energy rises through the setup.

beats.name: Apex
beats.job: Peak intensity of the film.

beats.name: Release
beats.job: Energy falls away.

beats.name: CTA
beats.job: A release, not a peak; hold still so the text can be read.

frameworks.notes: For 60 s the source only says apex near 0:40 and CTA from 0:50; its text says apex is two-thirds in, though the 30 s apex window ends there rather than centres on it. Sizes are the source's timings, allowed 25% either way.

frameworks.name: Short-form retention arc
frameworks.what: Vertical shorts (Reels, TikTok, Shorts) built around one idea and an open loop.

beats.name: Hook
beats.job: One frame plus one line that opens a loop.

beats.name: Setup
beats.job: Say why to watch: promise, stakes or the gap.

beats.name: Body
beats.job: Deliver value one idea per beat with a visual change every 2-4 s.

beats.name: Payoff and loop
beats.job: Close the loop, or feed the last frame back to frame one.

frameworks.notes: Budget is for a 20 s short; the source says scale the body and keep the 1 s hook, so shares for 60 s would differ. Sizes are the source's timings, allowed 25% either way.

frameworks.name: Reel shape (hook, stake, body, payoff)
frameworks.what: 15 to 45 s vertical Reels or similar shorts from one spoken script.

beats.name: Hook
beats.job: The claim, with motion in the first frame and its text up at frame one.

beats.name: The stake
beats.job: Why this matters to the viewer, one line.

beats.name: Body
beats.job: One idea per beat and a changing frame each beat.

beats.name: Payoff, ask and loop
beats.job: Deliver the hook's promise, one ask, and echo a word from the hook.

frameworks.notes: Source gives hook 0-2 s, stake 2-7 s and a payoff in the last 3 s; the script flags a hook past 3 s and any single beat past 4 s. beats.py itself is a script timer, not a template. Sizes are the source's timings, allowed 25% either way.

frameworks.name: Long-form skeleton with sag re-hook
frameworks.what: Long YouTube films of about 10 to 12 minutes built as a chain of open loops.

beats.name: Hook
beats.job: Stop the click-away and make a promise within the first 30 s.

beats.name: Setup
beats.job: Frame the stakes and preview the payoff.

beats.name: Body, first chapters
beats.job: Deliver value as a loop chain; open the next loop before closing one.

beats.name: Sag point re-hook
beats.job: Re-hook before the 40-60% drop with a twist, raised stakes or restated promise.

beats.name: Body, later chapters
beats.job: Keep chaining loops; alternate dense information with story.

beats.name: Payoff
beats.job: Resolve the opening loop explicitly and echo the hook.

beats.name: Outro and CTA
beats.job: One action only plus a next-video tease.

frameworks.notes: Source times assume 10-12 min; hook at most 30 s and outro at most 15 s at any length. The payoff start (0.9) is my assumption; source says only near the end. Sizes are the source's timings, allowed 25% either way.
